rule.name: SuppressionNeedsJustification
rule.message: A @SuppressWarnings must be accompanied by @Justification stating why the suppressed rule does not apply here.
rule.description: A suppression records that a rule was consciously set aside. Without the reason, a later reader cannot tell a considered exception from a silenced defect, so the suppression becomes permanent by default. Pairing every @SuppressWarnings with @Justification keeps the reason in the code. The annotation has SOURCE retention and is filtered out of the executable jar.

rule.name: JustificationNeedsText
rule.message: A @Justification reason must contain non-whitespace text.
rule.description: A present but blank reason is indistinguishable from no reason and must not satisfy the suppression policy.

rule.name: JustificationNeedsSuppression
rule.message: A @Justification without @SuppressWarnings is stale; remove the explanation with the suppression it used to justify.
rule.description: A justification exists only to explain one suppression. Once that suppression is removed, retaining the annotation leaves an explanation for an exception the code no longer takes and makes the declaration look exceptional when it is not.

rule.name: PairedConditionParentheses
rule.message: A multiline if/while condition must start on the line after '(' and end on the line before ')'.
rule.description: Extends paired-parentheses notation to if and while conditions. A one-line condition stays compact; once the condition spans lines, the opening parenthesis ends its line, the condition occupies the inner lines, and the closing parenthesis starts the following line.

property.name: xpath
property.value: (//IfStatement | //WhileStatement)[ let $condition := *[1], $body := *[2], $opening := pmd:startLine(.), $first := pmd:startLine($condition), $last := pmd:endLine($condition), $closing := pmd:startLine($body) return ($opening != $first or $first != $last or $last != $closing) and ( $opening = $first or $last = $closing ) ]

rule.name: UninitializedLocalVariable
rule.message: Don't declare a local variable without an initializer in order to assign it later, e.g. in the branches of a 'try/catch' or 'if/else' statement. Initialize the variable at the declaration or return directly from every branch. Suppress this rule explicitly in the rare cases where the deferred assignment is genuinely the most reasonable approach.
rule.description: Locals declared without an initializer and assigned later (typically once per branch) add indirection that hides the fact that every branch fully determines the value. Initialize at the declaration or return directly from every branch instead.

rule.name: NoThrowsInTestClass
rule.message: A test class must not declare a 'throws' clause on a method or constructor; annotate it with Lombok's @SneakyThrows instead so the test signature stays free of checked-exception boilerplate.
rule.description: In a class whose name ends with 'Test', a method or constructor that declares checked exceptions with a 'throws' clause adds boilerplate that carries no test-level meaning (an unexpected checked exception simply fails the test). Use Lombok's @SneakyThrows on the method instead of a 'throws' clause.

rule.name: NoAbbreviatedNames
rule.message: A name in this declaration abbreviates a word; spell it out (see this rule's description for the list).
rule.description:
A reader should not have to expand an abbreviation to know what a name holds, and a codebase that abbreviates some names and not others makes the reader wonder whether the difference means something. The list below is the one eslint-plugin-unicorn replaces, minus the entries that do not survive the move to Java: application, applications, configuration and repository, which that list maps to app, apps, config and repo and which Java spells out; and args, because the JVM itself declares main(String... args).
A word is checked wherever it falls in a camelCase name, so logsDir fails as surely as dir. The check covers what this project declares (locals, parameters, fields and its own methods) and not what it calls, since a name in a library or an inherited signature is not ours to spell.
acc, arg, arr, attr, attrs, btn, buf, cb, cfg, cmd, conf, ctx, cur, curr, db, decl, decls, def, dep, deps, dest, dev, dir, dirs, dist, doc, docs, dst, e, el, elem, elems, env, envs, err, ev, evt, expr, exprs, ext, exts, fn, func, i, ident, idents, idx, j, len, lib, mod, msg, num, obj, opts, param, params, perf, pkg, prev, prod, prop, props, proto, ref, refs, rel, req, res, ret, retval, sep, src, stdDev, stmt, stmts, str, tbl, temp, tit, tmp, util, utils, val, var, vars, ver

rule.name: NativeQueryNeedsJustification
rule.message: A native query is a deliberate exception. Suppress this rule and state in @Justification why JPQL does not answer here.
rule.description:
A native query ties the application to one database dialect and bypasses the persistence context, so the entities it returns are outside whatever the surrounding transaction is tracking. It is sometimes the right answer and never an accidental one, which is the shape the suppression policy already has a mechanism for. The pair that answers it is @SuppressWarnings with @Justification beside it, which keeps the reason next to the query and prices it against the same budget every other deliberate exception is priced against.
The rule therefore reports a justified query as well as an unjustified one, and that is what makes the pair possible at all. A rule that fell silent at the sight of the reason would leave the suppression suppressing nothing, which UnnecessaryWarningSuppression refuses and no suppression can answer, and a justification with no suppression beside it, which JustificationNeedsSuppression refuses. Between the three of them a native query could not be written in any form.
The value is read rather than the member, because a query stating nativeQuery = false states that it is not one.
The rule needs no Spring file pattern. Nothing outside Spring Data writes this attribute, so a project that is not a Spring Boot one never reaches the rule at all.
